skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-meta-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Configure Meta Ads to value paid repeat orders from Lightspeed eCom (C-Series). Use Product Metrics to check customer classification, test conversion delivery, and guide manual setup in Meta.
skill.summary: Set up and verify revenue or profit conversion tracking for repeat Lightspeed orders in Meta Ads.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown formatting, normal account setup, or passive links. Confirmed risks include unpinned installation, mutable remote instructions, authenticated writes, and broad order reads. The review also found unsafe credential guidance, broader live event sharing than the task implies, and a conflicting profit conversion rule.

remediation.issue: The skill can request API credentials and pass them through agent tools.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the verified Product Metrics app or a dedicated secret input. Never solicit credentials in chat or include them in model-visible tool arguments.

remediation.issue: Live Meta setup can send more events and data than the repeat-order workflow implies.
remediation.suggestion: Keep delivery paused or in test mode until the merchant confirms the pixel, event types, shared fields, consent settings, and start of live reporting.

remediation.issue: The workflow can write settings or retrieve order records without specifying the exact approved scope.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the company, storefront, and intended write before execution. Limit order reads to the requested sample and return classifications without identifiers or margins unless needed.

remediation.issue: The installer and remote workflow depend on content outside the reviewed revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer and skill revision, and ship reviewed references. Restrict MCP calls to approved operations and validate browser URLs before presenting them.

remediation.issue: The main instructions and returning-customer reference use different profit events.
remediation.suggestion: Use PMReturningCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_RETURNING_PROFIT throughout this workflow. Verify both fields before advising the merchant to select the conversion.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant Solicits Integration Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The main rules allow the assistant to request raw integration secrets and pass them to a command. The Meta guide both advises app entry and says the assistant must ask for the token. This route can expose credentials in conversation, tool records, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exception and command handoff are explicit. Lightspeed documents write access to tracking and settings, but no credential capture was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Live Meta Setup Sends Broader Customer Data
semantic_findings.description: The setup leaves Meta sending on and makes test mode optional. The destination also sends checkout, purchase, and other conversion events with matching data when consent allows. The repeat-order workflow does not require separate merchant confirmation of that broader transfer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide documents the sending setting and wider event payloads. Shopper consent controls are described, but they do not confirm the merchant intended that scope.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Guidance Uses an All-Order Conversion
semantic_findings.description: The main instructions recommend PMOrderProfit with ORDER_PROFIT. The returning-customer guide specifies PMReturningCustomerProfit with CUSTOMER_RETURNING_PROFIT. Following the main instructions could make a retention ad set optimize for orders beyond its intended audience.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guides specify distinct event and purpose pairs, and the Meta guide lists general profit separately from returning-customer events.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for Repeat Lightspeed Orders
content.value_statement: Standard purchase events do not distinguish repeat orders from first purchases. Use Product Metrics to verify repeat-order signals and set up a dedicated Meta conversion.
actual_capabilities: Check whether the selected Lightspeed shop and property have active server-side tracking to Meta.
Review recent paid orders to identify new, returning, and unknown customer classifications.
Guide setup of the repeat-order revenue or profit conversion in Meta Events Manager.
Explain how to verify delivery with a paid repeat test order and a Meta test event code.
Identify common blockers such as incomplete costs, missing consent, or a saved test event code.
limitations: Requires Lightspeed eCom (C-Series), a proxied Cloudflare storefront, and a Product Metrics Pro workspace.
A person must create the custom conversion in Meta and select it for the ad set.
The profit event requires complete order costs and active additional costs.
Past orders are not imported. Later refunds do not revise events already sent to Meta.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify which store, gateway, and Meta connection steps remain before testing repeat orders.

use_cases.title: Set a Retention Conversion
use_cases.description: Choose a revenue or profit conversion for a retention ad set and verify the event before selecting it.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing Repeat Events
use_cases.description: Check customer classification, test mode, consent, and cost completeness to explain missing conversion activity.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need to set up repeat-order bidding for my Lightspeed shop in Meta? Give me a checklist. Do not request credentials or make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recent Classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm my company and storefront before checking the last 20 paid orders. Report counts for new, returning, and unknown. Do not include customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Revenue Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through a paid repeat test order with marketing and analytics consent. Tell me what to verify in Meta Test events. Leave live settings unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Profit Conversion
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my repeat-order profit setup without changing it. Verify cost completeness, the event and purpose rule, and the intended ad set. Flag any mismatch before launch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Before switching a retention ad set to profit

output_examples.input: What do the classifications from my 20-order review show?
output: Of 20 paid orders, 8 were returning, 10 were new, and 2 were unknown.
The unknown orders lacked enough customer history for classification. Do not count them as returning.

output_examples.input: My paid repeat test order reached Meta. What should I verify next?
output: For revenue, check that the event is PMReturningCustomer and the purpose is CUSTOMER_RETURNING.
Create the custom conversion in Events Manager. Confirm the pixel and consent settings before you remove the test event code and begin live reporting.

best_practices: Enter API keys, secrets, and access tokens directly in the verified Product Metrics app.
Use a paid test order from an existing test customer with marketing and analytics consent.
Confirm the destination, shared data, and event purpose before starting live delivery or selecting the conversion.
anti_patterns: Do not use a general purchase or profit event when the campaign should optimize only for repeat orders.
Do not assume an active connection proves Meta received the correct event.
Do not paste credentials or identifiable order details into chat.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed shops are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers Lightspeed eCom (C-Series) stores in the Europe and United States clusters.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics identify returning customers?
faq.answer: It uses Lightspeed's new-customer flag and order history. An earlier order makes the customer returning.

faq.question: Why is the returning-customer event missing in Meta?
faq.answer: Meta must receive the event before listing it. Test with a paid repeat order and accept marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Can I optimize for profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the returning-customer profit event and its matching purpose rule. Product Metrics needs complete costs to send the profit event.

faq.question: Does the skill change my ad set in Meta?
faq.answer: No. The skill guides you through the setup. You select the custom conversion in Meta Ads Manager.

faq.question: Are old orders imported into Meta?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics sends orders from the time tracking goes live. Meta rejects events older than seven days.
